text:
The stock fell just 0.07% today—essentially flat—after a strong 5.3% rally over the past two weeks. The tiny move today likely reflects consolidation after yesterday's sharp 3.3% jump to $134.19, which coincided with news of Trump's diesel deal with Putin aimed at easing U.S. fuel prices by tapping Russian supply.

The two-week rally reflects the broader oil market backdrop: crude is trading at $125 per barrel globally (versus $96 domestically), and multiple supply disruptions are supporting prices—Hurricane Isaias hit Gulf of Mexico production, tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are surging to wartime highs, and ongoing Middle East and Ukraine conflicts have already damaged refining capacity worldwide. For an oil company, higher global crude prices and tighter fuel markets are favorable, even as geopolitical tensions and production risks create volatility day-to-day.
